STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.claim: The narrative recounts the destruction of Shuʿayb's people after their rejection of him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.claim: The promised messenger mission continued, and the accounts of those messengers are set out in verses 59–92.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.anchor: Then in accordance with this promise, He continued to send messengers. Its details are stated in verses 59-92 ahead.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.claim: Section VI reinforces warnings of the Hereafter to Quraysh with Arabian nations’ histories: they received political authority, became ungrateful and unjust, rejected messengers and were destroyed after respite. Quraysh face the same situation and impending judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.anchor: The purpose of narrating these anecdotes to the Quraysh is that they too are facing the same situation and their fate is about to be decided by God’s court of justice

STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.claim: The account of Midian's destruction matches the account of the Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ.
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.anchor: The description of the destruction of the Midianites is identical to that of the Thamūd

STUDYQURAN:7:91/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r2.claim: A report says God first sent Midian oppressive heat, then a cooling cloud that drew the people together before fire, a terrible cry, and an earthquake killed them.
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r2.anchor: It is reported that when the people of Midian denied Shuʿayb, God first sent upon them such a terrible heat

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r6.claim: The phrase 'they became in the morning' means either that they became so or that morning came upon them; its meaning was explained earlier in the parallel account of Salih's people.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r6.anchor: أصبحوا أي صاروا أو دخلوا في الصباح

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.claim: Though deeply established in their land, Shu'ayb's people abandoned it and all they owned in an instant when the quake left them crouched dead in their homes; their confidence that he and his followers would be driven out was reversed.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.anchor: وقد ترك هؤلاء وهم أمة عريقة في الأرض دارهم وما فيها

TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.claim: The sequence overturns the chiefs' boast: the punishment first leaves its victims implicit, then 7:92 names the deniers as those destroyed and truly made losers, contrary to their claim about Shu'ayb's followers.
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر نزول العذاب وأبهم الذين أخذتهم الرجفة فقال { فأخذتهم الرجفة } ولم يقل فأخذت الذين كفروا الرجفة

TABRISI:7:90-93/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r10.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:7:90-93/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the affliction as an earthquake that seized Shuayb's people.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r10.anchor: فأخذ قوم شعيب الزلزلة عن الكلبي

TABRISI:7:90-93/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين
TABRISI:7:90-93/r11.claim: In the Day of the Canopy account, scorching heat drove them indoors without relief; a cool, fragrant cloud drew them outside, where it burned them as the earth shook, leaving them like fried locusts and then ashes.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r11.anchor: وهو عذاب يوم الظلة عن ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين

TABRISI:7:90-93/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله ع
TABRISI:7:90-93/r12.claim: Abu Abdillah reports that God sent one cry against them and they died.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r12.anchor: وقيل: بعث الله عليهم صيحة واحدة فماتوا عن أبي عبد الله ع

TABRISI:7:90-93/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r13.claim: An alternative account distinguishes two peoples of Shuayb: one was destroyed by the quake and another was the people of the Canopy.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r13.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان لشعيب قومان قوم أهلكوا بالرجفة وقوم هم أصحاب الظلة

TABRISI:7:90-93/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r14.claim: They were found dead, lying face down in their dwellings.

THALABI:v4p261#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p261#2/r15.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p261#2/r15.claim: Al-Kalbi explains الرجفة as an earthquake.

THALABI:v4p261#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p261#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره من المفسرين
THALABI:v4p261#2/r16.claim: They report the Day of the Canopy: unbearable heat drove people from their homes to a cooling cloud, which God set ablaze as the ground shook, burning them to ash.
THALABI:v4p261#2/r16.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وغيره من المفسرين: فتح الله عليهم بابا من أبواب جهنم فأرسل عليهم ريحا

THALABI:v4p261#2/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p261#2/r17.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v4p261#2/r17.claim: Abu al-Aliya says دارهم means their dwellings or homes.

THALABI:v4p261#2/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p261#2/r18.speaker: محمد بن مروان
THALABI:v4p261#2/r18.claim: Muhammad ibn Marwan says Quranic دارهم means their destruction, while ديارهم means their armies.
THALABI:v4p261#2/r18.anchor: وقال محمد بن مروان: كل شيء في القرآن (دارهم) فهو [مرغمهم]

THALABI:v4p263/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v4p263/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports a story received about Umar ibn Jalhaʾ from Midian, who saw the wrath-bearing cloud and warned that Shuaib was sent and the cloud signaled doom; Samir and Imran were their soothsayers and al-Raqim their dog.
THALABI:v4p263/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: بلغني أن رجلا من أهل مدين يقال له عمر بن [جلهاء]

THALABI:v4p263/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله البجلي
THALABI:v4p263/r2.claim: Al-Bajali says the Abjad letter names were kings' names and their king ruled in Shuaib's time; Kalmun's sister laments his fiery death beneath the cloud.
THALABI:v4p263/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله البجلي: أبجد وهوز وحطي وكلمن وسعفص وقرشت: أسماء ملوك

ELMALILI:7:91/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:91/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:91/r1.claim: Jāthimīn describes them crouched on their chests with legs folded like sleeping rabbits or birds, pressed to the ground and unable to move.
ELMALILI:7:91/r1.anchor: Tavşanın ve kuşun uyuduğu vaziyet gibi ayakların iki sâkı kabzolunarak göğsü üzerine yere çöküp yapışmaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.claim: Madyan’s unbelieving, oppressive elite threatened Shuʿayb’s people, but suffered their deserved catastrophe and vanished as if no one had lived there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.anchor: asıl kendileri hak ettikleri büyük felâkete uğramışlar; bu dünyada öyle bir topluluk yaşamamış gibi yok olup gitmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.claim: Because Shuʿayb had done everything to rescue them from error and avert this fate, there was no reason to pity them afterward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.anchor: Şuayb, daha önce onları dalâletten kurtarmak ve böyle bir âkıbete mâruz kalmalarını önlemek için elinden gelen her şeyi yaptığından

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.claim: The preceding accounts of five prophets are concise lessons about their calls, people's responses, and the disasters suffered by oppressors, rather than history for its own sake.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.anchor: beş peygamberin kendi toplumlarıyla ilişkileri, davetlerinin mahiyeti, bu davet karşısında inanan ve inanmayanların tutumları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.claim: The ensuing verses present communities' calamities and hardships as having the purpose of reforming people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.anchor: Müteakip âyetlerde ise bütün bu toplumların uğradığı felâketlerin, zorlukların insanları ıslah etmeye yönelik amaçlar taşıdığı bildirilmektedir

ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r4.anchor: وقوله جل وعز: (فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين). أي أجساما ملقاة في الأرض كالرماد الجاثم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r5.claim: They lay as bodies cast on the ground, like settled ash.
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r5.anchor: وقوله جل وعز: (فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين). أي أجساما ملقاة في الأرض كالرماد الجاثم.

ASAD-NOTES:7:88#n73/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:88#n73/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:88#n73/r1.claim: Like the Thamud-inhabited harrah, the adjoining region of Madyan (Biblical Midian) shows abundant evidence of volcanic eruptions and earthquakes.
ASAD-NOTES:7:88#n73/r1.anchor: Like the harrah once inhabited by the Thamud tribe, the adjoining region of Madyan (the Biblical Midian) shows ample evidence of volcanic eruptions and earthquakes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.claim: God's law applies equally to every nation: after a messenger comes, a people must accept reform or face destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.anchor: When God sends a messenger to a nation, it is faced with either of the two options: to accept reformation or be put to death.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.claim: Arabs knew these nations' stories through vague traditions, especially lacking their moral lessons; the Qur’an restores that history and tells Quraysh to learn that these are their own warning stories.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.anchor: Their moral aspect, in particular, was totally ambiguous. The Qur’ ān has lifted the veil from this ambiguity and revived their history.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The warning to Quraysh begins with accounts of peoples known across Arabia's north, south, and northwest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: those nations are taken up which became famous while inhabiting the north, the south and the north west of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The nations in these accounts were destroyed for denying their messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: All of them were destroyed because they denied their respective messengers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The accounts follow historical order, so Noah's nation is treated first.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: The sequence adopted is historical. For this reason, the nation of Noah (sws) is taken up the first.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.claim: The wording of the punishment occurs identically in the account of Salih’s people and states the punishment without specifying its nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.anchor: The second of the verses occurs in precisely the same words in the anecdote of the nation of Ṣāliḥ.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.claim: Hud 11:94 explains the punishment with al-sayhah, meaning a shout and thunder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.anchor: which means a shout and thunder.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.claim: Shuara 26:189 calls it the torment of the day of the canopy; viewed from afar, it looked like a column or mountain of dust or smoke.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.anchor: It is evident from this that looking from afar, the torment seemed like a column or mountain of dust or smoke.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.claim: Islahi relates the torment of Lot’s people to a stone-hurling wind and says the ḥāṣib punishment combines rajfah, sayhah, and zullah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.anchor: It is evident from the anecdote of Lot’s nation that it was visited by a

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.claim: Another Qur’anic passage indicates that Madyan suffered the same punishment as Lot’s people; Islahi begins citing Shuayb’s warning in Hud 11:89.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p80/.anchor: From another instance of the Qur’ān also, it is evident that the same torment visited them as the one that visited Lots’ nation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.claim: Shuʿayb’s people suffer the same fate as Lot’s nearby people, linking this account to the earlier Lot narrative.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.anchor: It is evident from the last verse that Shu‘ayb’s nation too met the same fate

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and others report that unbearable heat drove the people from their homes into the open; they gathered beneath a cool cloud, which trapped and burned them as the earth shook, leaving them ashes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: لما دعى عليهم فتح عليهم باب من جهنم بحر شديد أخذ بأنفاسهم فلم ينفعهم ظل ولا ماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r4.claim: An unattributed report says the wind was withheld from them for seven days and then intense heat was sent against them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r4.anchor: وروي أن الريح حبست عنهم سبعة أيام ثم سلط عليهم الحر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r5.speaker: يزيد الجريري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r5.claim: Yazid al-Jariri says wind was sent on them for seven days; they then gathered under a distant mountain with springs and streams, and it fell on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r5.anchor: وقال يزيد الجريري: سلط عليهم الريح سبعة أيام ثم رفع لهم جبل من بعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r6.claim: Qatada distinguishes the people of the Thicket, destroyed by the cloud, from the people of Midian, destroyed by Gabriel's shout.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: أرسل شعيب إلى أصحاب الأيكة فأهلكوا بالظلة وإلى أصحاب مدين فصاح بهم جبريل صيحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows that one group of Shuaib's people died by the earthquake and another by the cloud-shade.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن فرقة من قوم شعيب هلكت بالرجفة وفرقة هلكت بالظلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r8.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says he had heard that when Amr ibn Jalha saw the cloud he recited a warning poem; its ending says only their dog al-Ruqaym would walk among the mountain passes, with Simir and Imran identified as their soothsayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r8.anchor: وقال الطبري بلغني أن رجلا منهم يقال له عمرو بن جلها لما رأى الظلة. قال الشاعر: يا قوم إن شعيبا مرسل فذروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله البجلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r9.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Bajali says the abjad letter names were kings of Midian and Kalman ruled when the punishment came in Shuaib's time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r9.anchor: وعن أبي عبد الله البجلي: أبو جاد وهوز وحطي وكلمن وسعفص وقرشت أسماء ملوك مدين وكان كلمن ملكهم يوم نزول العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r10.speaker: ابنة كلمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r10.claim: Kalman's daughter mourns him as the people's lord who died in fire beneath a cloud, with the flames making their home disappear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116/r10.anchor: فلما هلك قالت ابنته تبكيه: كلمن قد هد ركني ... هلكه وسط المحله سيد القوم أتاه ... حتف نار وسط ظله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī explains rajfa as an earthquake.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r2.claim: The “cry” in 11:94 may have been a precursor to the earthquake; destruction is attributed sometimes to its immediate and sometimes to its more distant cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r2.anchor: ولعلها كانت من مبادي الرجفة فأسند إهلاكهم إلى السبب القريب تارة وإلى البعيد أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r3.claim: Some distinguish two peoples addressed by Shuʿayb: Midian was destroyed by earthquake and al-Ayka by the cry; al-Ālūsī says this only works if Midian was not also destroyed by the cry, while Qatāda assigns Midian the cry and al-Ayka the cloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن القصة غير واحدة فإن شعيبا عليه السلام بعث إلى أمتين أهل مدين وأهل الأيكة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r4.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Midian first suffered intense heat, then gathered beneath a cool, pleasant cloud; fire consumed them there as the earth shook, leaving ash.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r4.anchor: فقد روي عن ابن عباس وغيره في هذه الآية إن الله تعالى فتح عليهم بابا من جهنم فأرسل عليهم حرا شديدا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r5.speaker: عبد الله البجلي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r5.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh al-Bajalī says King Kilmān died on the day of the cloud and his daughter mourned him in verse, apparently conflicting with the death of all; she may have been a believing survivor.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r5.anchor: عن عبدالله البجلي قال : كان أبو جاد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that the report about Kilmān’s daughter may lack a reliable chain.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r6.anchor: وقد يقال : إن هذا الخبر مما ليس له سند يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6/r7.claim: The expression “lying motionless in their dwellings” was explained in an earlier parallel passage.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the rajfah as an earthquake.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and others tell that a gate of Hell opened and sent fierce heat; caves were hotter than outside, so the people fled under a cool cloud, then God set it ablaze and shook the earth, burning them to ash.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: فتح الله عليهم بابا من جهنم، فأرسل عليهم حرا شديدا، فأخذ بأنفاسهم ولم ينفعهم ظل ولا ماء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r6.claim: Another account says God withheld wind for seven days and then imposed heat on them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r6.anchor: وروي أن الله تعالى حبس عنهم الريح سبعة أيام ثم سلط عليهم الحر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r7.speaker: يزيد الجريري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r7.claim: Yazid al-Jurayri says heat afflicted them for seven days; they gathered under a distant mountain with streams and springs, which fell on them, fulfilling 26:189.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r7.anchor: قال يزيد الجريري: سلط الله عليهم الحر سبعة أيام ثم رفع لهم جبل من بعيد، فأتاه رجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r8.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r8.claim: Qatada distinguishes the people of the thicket, destroyed by the shade, from the people of Midian, destroyed by Gabriel’s cry.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: بعث الله شعيبا إلى أصحاب الأيكة وأصحاب مدين، أما أصحاب الأيكة فأهلكوا بالظلة، وأما أصحاب مدين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله البجلي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r9.claim: Abu Abdullah al-Bajali lists Midian’s kings and says Kalman ruled in Shuayb’s time during the day of the shade; Kalman’s daughter mourned him in verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p258/r9.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله البجلي: كان أبو جاد وهوز وحطي وكلمن وسعفص وقرشت ملوك مدين، وكان

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r1.claim: The rajfa was an earthquake; al-Ḥijr calls it a cry, which may have been the earthquake’s onset.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r2.claim: Their dār means their town or city.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:91/r2.anchor: في دارهم جثمين } أي في مدينتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r4.claim: The rajfa is a tremendous shaking of hearts or dwellings; the author allows that it caused the cry or resulted from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r4.anchor: أي الزلزلة العظيمة في القلوب أو الديار التي كانت سببا للصيحة أو مسببة عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r5.claim: They remained collapsed on their knees or fixed motionless in their dwellings; the singular 'their abode' has a previously discussed rhetorical secret.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r5.anchor: أي باركين على الركب أو لازمين أمكنتهم لا حراك بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r6.claim: He compares the punishment with reports of angels at Hunayn, unbelievers hearing a pebble-like sound within themselves, and an enemy feeling terror a month's journey in front and behind; for Muhammad, the prophet of mercy, this sign brought salvation rather than destruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r6.anchor: مثل وقع الحصاة في الطست , ودون ما كان يجد مخالفة من الرعب من مسيرة شهر

DURR-FULL:v3p501/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r6.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r6.claim: When the people persisted in rebellion, Gabriel stood among them and shouted; the mountains and earth shook, their souls left their bodies, and the trembling ground cast them down dead.
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r6.anchor: فلما عتوا على الله {أخذتهم الرجفة} وذلك أن جبريل نزل فوقف عليهم فصاح صيحة رجفت منها الجبال والأرض فخرجت أرواحهم من أبدانهم

DURR-FULL:v3p501/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r7.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r7.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Suddī say Shuʿayb was sent twice: Midian was destroyed by the cry, and the People of the Thicket by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy.
DURR-FULL:v3p501/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة والسدي قالا: ما بعث الله نبيا مرتين إلا شعيبا مرة إلى مدين فأخذهم الله بالصيحة ومرة أخرى إلى أصحاب الأيكة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses the quake as a cry.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : الرجفة قال : الصيحة . آية 91

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam glosses “crouching” as dead.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1523#2/r2.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : جاثمين قال : ميتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r1.claim: The fāʾ marks the punishment as following immediately after the leaders' warning to their people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r1.anchor: كان أخذ الرجفة إياهم عقب قولهم لقومهم ما قالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr points back to the parallel account of Thamūd's punishment in 7:78.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r3.claim: The people of Midian were struck by lightning from a cloud, the punishment called the “day of the shade” in 26:189.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r4.claim: Because Hūd's account calls it a cry, the sound is best understood as a splitting burst from a thing launched against another, not the impact sound of an earthquake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r4.anchor: وقد عبر عن الرجفة في سورة هود بالصيحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r5.claim: He prefers that both an earthquake and lightning struck them: the “quaking” was the earthquake and the “cry” the thunderbolt, consistent with the erased traces.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r5.anchor: والأظهر أن يكون أصابهم زلزال وصواعق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r2.claim: Al-rajfa is a powerful earthquake that makes a person shake, tremble, and convulse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r2.anchor: والرجفة الزلزلة الشديدة التي ينال معها الإنسان اهتزاز وارتعاد واضطراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r3.claim: The author allows that one group of Shuʿayb’s people died in the earthquake and another in the cloud, or that the earthquake and cloud struck together.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن فرقة من قوم شعيب أهلكت ب الرجفة وفرقة بالظلة ويحتمل أن الظلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r4.claim: Reports differ on whether Shuʿayb was sent to Midian and the people of al-Aykah as two peoples or as one people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r4.anchor: بعث شعيبا إلى أهل مدين وإلى أصحاب الأيكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r5.claim: An account says that after their prolonged defiance, intense heat from a gate of Hell overcame them; a pleasant breeze and cloud drew them together, then the cloud closed over and killed them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r5.anchor: فلما عتوا وطالت بهم المدة فتح الله عليهم بابا من أبواب جهنم فأهلكهم الحر منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r6.speaker: عمرو بن جلهاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that ʿAmr b. Jallaha saw the cloud and warned his people that Shuʿayb was a messenger and that the cloud signaled their death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r6.anchor: أن رجلا من أهل مدين يقال له عمرو بن جلهاء قال لما رآها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r7.claim: The poem’s Samir and ʿImran are the people’s soothsayers, and al-Raqim is their dog.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله البجلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits al-Bajalī’s account that the letter-names are Midianite kings and Kulman was king at the time of the cloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r10.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله البجلي أنه قال: أبو جاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r11.speaker: أخت كلمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p429/r11.claim: The account announces Kulman’s sister’s elegy, which says his death broke her support and that fire consumed the settlement beneath the cloud’s shade.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r1.claim: The author cautions that the story identifying Kulman and the other kings is speculative and God knows its truth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذه حكاية مظنون بها والله علم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r1.claim: The people of Shuʿayb were intensely unbelieving and defiant; they swore that following him would bring loss, immediately before the earthquake seized them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن شدة كفر قوم شعيب وتمردهم وعتوهم، وما هم فيه من الضلال،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r2.claim: They were shaken as they had shaken and threatened to expel Shuʿayb and his companions; Hūd describes their destruction by a blast instead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r2.anchor: أخبر تعالى هاهنا أنهم أخذتهم الرجفة كما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r3.claim: Their mockery of Shuʿayb's prayer and challenge for a piece of heaven to fall was answered by the cry and the punishment of the day of shadow; Ibn Kathīr says all these punishments came together.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r3.anchor: ثم جاءتهم صيحة من السماء ورجفة من الأرض شديدة من أسفل منهم، فزهقت الأرواح، وفاضت النفوس وخمدت الأجساد،

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r2.claim: Aṣbaḥa means entering the morning, just as amsā means entering the evening.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r2.anchor: والإصباح: الدخول في الصباح، كما أن الإمساء الدخول في المساء.

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r12.claim: The fāʾ is connective; the quake is the punishment answering the grave corruption they committed.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r12.anchor: كان جواب ما ارتكبوه من عظيم الفساد أخذ الرجفة لهم بالعذاب.

MUQATIL:7:90-93/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r2.anchor: { فأخذتهم الرجفة } ، يعنى العذاب، { فأصبحوا } من صيحة جبريل

MUQATIL:7:90-93/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r3.claim: They awoke in their village dead and extinguished after Gabriel's cry.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ فأخذتهم الرجفة ﴾ الزلزلة ﴿ فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين ﴾ ميتين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#2/r2.claim: They were lying dead in their homes.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r3.claim: Al-rajfa means an earthquake; another view identifies it as the blast.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r4.claim: The people of the Thicket were destroyed by the canopy, a punishment discussed later.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r4.anchor: وأصحاب الأيكة أهلكوا بالظلة، على ما يأتي.

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r1.claim: The rajfa was a severe earthquake; Hud calls their destruction a cry, possibly preceding the quake, so the end is attributed once to a near cause and once to a remote one.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r1.anchor: أي : الزلزلة الشديدة وهكذا في سورة العنكبوت

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth shook and severe heat struck; a cloud appeared, they sought its relief, and punishment poured on them there with Gabriel's cry.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : رجفت بهم الأرض وأصابهم حر شديد فرفعت لهم سحابة فخرجوا إليها

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r3.claim: Their دار is their town; Hud's parallel says في ديارهم.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r3.anchor: أي : صاروا في مدينتهم وفي سورة هود

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r4.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r4.claim: Al-Haddadi places them under the cloud near their homes, dead on faces and knees, fixed in place with no escape, as in the Canopy Day punishment.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r4.anchor: قال الحدادي : أي بقرب دارهم تحت الظلة كما قال تعالى : {فأخذهم عذاب يوم الظلة}

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r5.claim: One report says they burned beneath the cloud and became ash-like bodies lying on the ground.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r5.anchor: وروي أنهم احترقوا تحت السحابة فصاروا ميتين بمنزلة الرماد الجاثم

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r6.claim: A second Ibn Abbas report says heat drove them into houses without relief; they welcomed a cool cloud, then God burned them beneath it and shook the earth until they became ash like fried locusts.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : فتح الله عليهم بابا من جهنم فأرسل عليهم منه حرا شديدا

BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r7.claim: The Najmiyya reading says stubbornness made them see truth as falsehood and success as loss; their bodily end mirrored their inner state, spirits squatting in bodily abodes.
BURSEVI:v3p153#5/r7.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : من عنادهم رأوا الحق باطلا والباطل حقا والفلاح خسرانا

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
